newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech minister says has gas supply plan ready.
newsitem.headline: Czech minister says has gas supply plan ready.

text.p: Czech Industry and Trade Minister Vladimir Dlouhy said on Friday his ministry had finalised a plan on diversification of natural gas supplies, which at present come solely from Russia, and would submit it to the cabinet within two weeka.
"The material has been ready for over a week. I would like to debate it.... we are talking about the following days, maybe two weeks," Dlouhy told reporters at a news conference.

He did not elaborate on the content of the plan, which had been expected to be submitted to the government in January. He said the plan would first be debated at a special meeting of ministers before going to the full cabinet.
The Czechs have ended their dependance on Russian crude oil by building a new pipeline to Germany, but are still completely dependant on gas supplies from Russia's Gazprom.
Government representatives have held talks on limited deliveries from Norway, but no deal has been finalised.
The ministry is drawing up four options for securing gas supplies, but has given no details. No matter which plan is excepted, Russia is expected to remain the dominant supplier.
Ministry sources said the four options were:
* Purchasing all gas from Gazprom, using two different shipping routes, with a long-term agreement until 2016 and price guarantees until 1998.

* Purchasing some Russian gas indirectly through Dutch company Nederlandse Gasunie NV, and Germany's Wintershall, a subsidiary of BASF. Gasunie would start supplies in 1998, delivering up to two billion cubic metres in 2005, with the agreement lasting until 2014.
In case of a fall in Russian supplies, Gasunie would deliver its own gas through Wingas, a joint venture of Wintershall and Gazprom.

Wintershall offers a similar scheme, with deliveries through Wingas starting on January 1 next year, rising to one billion cubic metres in 2000, under a deal which would last until 2016. Negotiations with these firms are in the stage of initiating a supply contract.
* Finalising and maintaining the agreement for Norwegian gas, which has already had preliminary approval for this year, until 2017.
* A limited purchase from Mobil Europe Gas Inc, Germany's Brigitta Erdgas und Erdoel (BEB) and British Gas Plc.
The Czech Republic consumes around eight to nine billion cubic metres of gas per year, but volumes are expected to rise to some 12-13 billion cubic metres by the turn of the century.
